title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
prompt:
Design a class that tracks the k-th largest element in a growing stream:

- `KthLargest(int k, int[] nums)` — initialize with existing numbers
- `int add(int val)` — append a value, return the current k-th largest

The size-k min-heap pattern, kept alive between calls as a field.

tests.note: starts empty; k=1 means simply the max

hints: You only ever need the k largest values seen so far. Among those, which one is the answer?
Keep a min-heap field holding at most k values. Its top, the smallest of the k largest, is the k-th largest.
add: `heap.offer(val); if (heap.size() > k) heap.poll(); return heap.peek();`. The constructor can just call `add` for each initial number.

solution.explanation: The heap always holds the k largest values seen so far, so its minimum is the k-th largest. Reusing `add` in the constructor keeps that rule in one place. O(log k) per add, O(n log k) to build, O(k) space.
